title: Google AI Student Offer: Free for a Year, But Do Taiwan College Students Qualify? 4 Requirements
description:
Tempted by Google's announcement of a free year of the Google AI student offer? This video walks Taiwan college students through all four official documents at once: the announcement, the offer terms, the supported-countries list, and the Taiwan student page.

Using four requirements - identity, region, account, and deadline - it helps you judge for yourself whether Taiwan qualifies; then it works out what actually happens in month 13, after the offer ends; and finally, using sample data from our own tutorial, it walks through checking an AI note's citations.

My take: what matters isn't how much you save, it's whether you get auto-charged once the offer ends. The moment you redeem it, set a calendar reminder before it expires; and for any AI-generated notes you'll use for homework or exams, open the citations and check the source actually says that.

nm7d.text: The redemption deadline only sets when to apply, not when the offer ends.

tjdk.text: All four requirements must hold at once to truly qualify.

bdvv.text: Of the four, the first two test your eligibility.

ztfc.text: The last one tests whether you acted within the deadline.

f9gv.text: This last step is the part people overlook most in a free year.

bnzc.text: Do AI-generated study notes ever misquote their sources?

qk58.text: Especially content you'll use for homework or exams.

6b4h.text: A prompt like this sets both the scope and the pass criteria.

22ic.text: It also has to flag which fields were corrected and which are still missing.

hqj8.text: Here's the table with the verified correct answers.

rdvu.text: The time, though, stayed 2pm in both - no change at all.

898w.text: This row is easy to mistake as also corrected - that's the error to catch.

aucr.text: If the AI marks this row as corrected too, it misread the source.

bbi7.text: The venue went from "TBD" to "community classroom" in the revision.

adye.text: From vague wording to a specific, named room.

9ege.text: Capacity went from about 20 to 24 - also corrected.

rdqg.text: The fee went from "TBD" to explicitly free in the revision.

a435.text: "TBD" doesn't mean paid - a field that's easy to misremember.

umgz.text: Neither announcement gives a registration deadline.

vaaq.text: Since neither states one, the AI shouldn't invent a date either.

nmn8.text: A citation number doesn't guarantee accuracy - clicking through is safest.

47yj.text: Back on that same Taiwan student page, three spots contradict each other.

3t34.text: Same page, three different corners, three different claims.

ic7q.text: The footer says 165 a month, promoting the Plus plan.

hwep.text: That line at the bottom is about pricing after the trial ends.

9q5n.text: The FAQ asks who gets it free, but answers "US college students."

yu5p.text: That summary might be the very first thing you see in search results.

7z8x.text: One page, three versions - even Google doesn't reconcile them.

5bdj.text: If Google itself can write three versions, one glance isn't enough to trust it.

7rde.text: After all this digging, what would I actually do?

938u.text: Before the conclusion, one thing I noticed.

67z6.text: It's actually the same lesson as today's demo.

8mxj.text: But the real point isn't how much you save.

kvy8.text: It's whether you end up paying once the offer ends.

5i2i.text: First: on redemption day, set a calendar reminder for just before it expires.

sr3p.text: The terms say it: if you don't cancel in time, the standard monthly fee kicks in.

weqg.text: That's written into the terms, not something support decides on the spot.

k946.text: Second: before it expires, actively decide whether to keep using it.

abrn.text: Don't trust yourself to remember - a reminder is more reliable.

ik8j.text: One calendar entry now beats disputing a charge later.

9m3b.text: Third is the thing I mentioned noticing - it's about AI notes.

93u7.text: In the same announcements, Google gives two answers on live voice chat.

ikea.text: The enterprise post says users 18+ can use it right now.

wths.text: But the consumer post says it's "coming soon."

y4ux.text: Same feature, two official documents, two different answers.

tigk.text: If Google's own press releases don't agree, AI notes can get things wrong too.

62qa.text: So third: open the citation on every AI-generated note and check it.

8p2f.text: Sounding plausible doesn't mean the source actually says that.

g4zn.text: Ten seconds checking beats finding out later it was wrong.
